steps.name: Install package with dev extras (pip install -e .[dev])
Install build tools (pip install --upgrade build twine)
Check distribution artifacts (python -m twine check dist/*)

secret_handling.token_scope: env-var local to Publish to PyPI step only (env: PYPI_API_TOKEN)
notes: Token is injected as a step-scoped env var, not exported at job or workflow level.
No echo, cat, or print of the token is present anywhere in the file.
PYPI_API_TOKEN is not written to any file or artifact.
GitHub automatically masks secret values in logs even if accidentally echoed; defense-in-depth.

Using -p "$PYPI_API_TOKEN" on the CLI technically passes the token as a process argument, which may be visible in /proc/<pid>/cmdline on Linux. Preferred alternative: use TWINE_PASSWORD env var instead of -p flag. Classified as low-risk finding — process args are masked by GitHub runner but worth noting.
contents:write is required for softprops/action-gh-release@v2 to create the GitHub Release and upload artifacts.
No id-token:write is present — OIDC trusted publishing is NOT used. Token-based auth only.
No packages:write or other elevated permissions are set.
Permissions are minimal for the declared purpose.
Neither the 'test' nor 'publish' job declares an 'environment:' key.
This means there is NO manual-approval gate before the PyPI upload step.
Any tag matching v*.*.* pushed to the repo will trigger a publish attempt immediately after tests pass.
For a pre-release (alpha/RC) workflow this is by design but operators should be aware that accidental tag pushes will trigger a live PyPI upload if the token is set.

tag_glob_analysis.explanation: GitHub Actions uses fnmatch-style globs for tag patterns. The pattern 'v*.*.*' splits on literal dots. The first segment 'v*' matches 'v0', the second '*' matches '1', and the third '*' matches '0a1' (wildcards are greedy and match any characters including alphanumerics). Therefore 'v0.1.0a1' is matched.

workflow_dispatch_analysis.impact: There is no manual trigger. Publish can only be initiated by pushing a tag. This reduces accidental publish risk from manual UI clicks but provides no emergency re-run capability without re-tagging.

publish_behavior.if_token_set: Runs test job (ruff + mypy + pytest) -> publish job: builds wheel+sdist, validates with twine check, attaches artifacts to GitHub Release, uploads to PyPI.
publish_behavior.if_token_unset: Runs test job -> publish job: builds wheel+sdist, validates with twine check, attaches artifacts to GitHub Release. PyPI upload step is skipped (if-condition evaluates false). No upload occurs.

findings.detail: PYPI_API_TOKEN is passed as a CLI argument via -p "$PYPI_API_TOKEN". Process arguments may be visible in /proc/<pid>/cmdline on Linux before they are masked. The safer pattern is to set TWINE_PASSWORD as a step env var and omit the -p flag entirely, as twine reads TWINE_PASSWORD automatically. GitHub runner log masking still protects log output, so actual exposure risk is very low.

No 'environment:' declaration on the publish job means there is no required-reviewer gate before PyPI publish. For a 0.1.0a1 alpha this is acceptable, but consider adding 'environment: pypi' with required reviewers for stable releases.

There is no workflow_dispatch trigger. Manual re-runs without a tag push are not possible. If a publish fails mid-way (e.g., twine check passes but upload fails), re-running requires deleting and re-pushing the tag.

Actions are pinned to major version tags (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-python@v5, softprops/action-gh-release@v2) rather than immutable SHA digests. This allows supply-chain risk if action maintainers push malicious commits to the tag. Low risk for these well-audited actions but SHA pinning is best practice.
